docs#MulEquiv.trans is a useful function that produces M ≃* P given the hypotheses h1 : M ≃* N and h2 : N ≃* P.

I tend to suspect that this is done by composing the functions contained in those two other MulEquivs. I'd prefer to write h2 ∘ h1 instead of h1.trans h2, but I notice that this doesn't work. Composition of MulEquivs produces an ordinary function, not another MulEquiv.

(Actually, what I'd really like is to have some composition notation going in the other direction, something like h1 ∘→ h2 -- I don't have an opinion on what symbol(s) might be used -- since that is the direction of 'flow' when composing the functions.)

I can easily believe that there are typing concerns (or compiler concerns?) that explain why things haven't been done this way, but I'd like to hear more about what those concerns might be.
There was a similar discussion in the past #mathlib4 > RFC: notation typeclass for composition
Can you use docs#Monoid.End instead? That has composition notated as *

Michael said:

I can easily believe that there are typing concerns (or compiler concerns?) that explain why things haven't been done this way, but I'd like to hear more about what those concerns might be.

I don't think this is the case. My experiments with these things have not uncovered any real problems (only issues that were problematic before), see for instance #41224
I don't have the energy to push this issue. A related issue is that .symm should be a notation typeclass as well.

Yakov Pechersky said:

Can you use docs#Monoid.End instead? That has composition notated as *

But that only works for M ≃* M
We have ≪≫ₗ for docs#LinearEquiv.trans. Maybe we should add ≪≫* for docs#MulEquiv.trans ?
We also have ∘ₗ for docs#LinearMap.comp, but not other types of morphisms.
